title: Binary Search
learningObjectives: Understand how to efficiently search a sorted array by eliminating half the search space.
intuition: If you are looking for a word in a dictionary, you don't start at page 1 and read every word (Linear Search). You open the middle, see if the word comes before or after, and eliminate half the book immediately. When can I eliminate half the search space? Only when the data is SORTED.
formalModel: f(A, target) = i if A[i] == target else -1. Let L=0, R=n-1. While L<=R, mid = L+(R-L)/2...
recognitionSignals: Sorted array, requirement for O(log n) time complexity, 'find a value', 'find a boundary'.
derivation: 1. Need bounds: left and right. 2. Find middle element. 3. Compare middle with target. 4. If target < middle, eliminate right half (right = mid - 1). 5. If target > middle, eliminate left half (left = mid + 1). 6. Repeat until left > right.
pseudocode:
L = 0, R = A.length - 1
while L <= R:
  mid = L + (R-L)/2
  if A[mid] == target return mid
  if A[mid] < target L = mid + 1
  else R = mid - 1
return -1
complexity: Time: O(log N) worst/average, O(1) best. Space: O(1).
correctness: Loop invariant: if the target is in the array, it must be in the range [left, right]. The search space strictly decreases each iteration because mid is excluded.
edgeCases: Empty array, array with 1 element, target smaller than all elements, target larger than all elements, even number of elements.
misconceptions: Believing Binary Search works on unsorted arrays. Calculating mid as (left+right)/2 which causes integer overflow.
counterexamples: [5, 2, 8, 1]. Binary search for 1. Mid is 2. 1 < 2, search left [5]. Mid is 5. 1 != 5. Not found! Unsorted fails.
commonWrongApproaches: Using (left + right) / 2 instead of left + (right - left) / 2. Using left < right instead of left <= right. Setting left = mid instead of mid + 1, causing infinite loops.
comparisonWithAlternatives: Linear Search: O(N) time but works on unsorted. Binary Search: O(log N) time but REQUIRES sorting. When you need multiple searches, sorting once (O(N log N)) and binary searching multiple times is optimal.
practiceProblems: 1. Classic Binary Search, 2. First Bad Version, 3. Search Insert Position.
transferProblem: Suppose you have an array that increases and then decreases (a mountain array). Can you still use the 'eliminate half' concept to find the peak? Why?
retrievalPrompt: What is the exact condition required to eliminate half the search space in an array, and how do you safely calculate the midpoint in Java?
